content: The Credit Cards dataset covers 1,351,919 transactions across 5,139 cards held by 4,000 customers, recorded between June 1, 2024 and May 31, 2026 (24 months).

The transactions table keys on card_id, not customer_id. To analyze spend or campaigns by customer (CIBIL band, income band, tenure), join transactions → cards → customers on card_id then customer_id.
Card portfolio status: 3,783 active (73.6%), 942 closed (18.3%), and 414 dormant (8.1%) of 5,139 cards. Closed + dormant together represent ~26% attrition/inactivity — a core retention metric.

Product mix is led by Select (1,294 cards), POP-CLUB (975), and ELITE+ (926), then Klick (837) and BankBazaar FinBooster (470). Premium tiers YES PREMIA (223), YES ELITE (148), and MARQUEE (33) are deliberately small, high-value cohorts.

Campaign funnel: of 53,227 contacts, 50,690 were ignored, 1,311 clicked without converting, 307 opted out, and 919 converted — a 1.7% conversion rate. This is a realistic range for credit-card cross-sell/upgrade campaigns.

Card revenue has four engines: interest on revolved balances, annual/late fees, foreign-exchange markup, and interchange on spend. In this data, ₹3.92 crore interest and ₹1.01 crore fees come from statements, plus ₹5.6 lakh forex markup from 3,667 international transactions.

27.6% of statements carry a revolving balance, and average credit utilization is 12.5%. Revolvers are a minority of accounts but drive the large majority of interest revenue, so revolve rate is the single most important profitability lever.

A clean cross-sell/upgrade journey for this data is: card issued → activated → spend begins → propensity signal fires → campaign sent → converted → upgrade or product cross-sell. Attribute conversions back to the originating propensity signal and campaign channel.

Propensity events (salary jump, travel-booking cluster, EMI-eligible big ticket, first international transaction, dormancy onset) are behavioral triggers that should precede a campaign. Conversion is far higher when a contact follows a fresh propensity signal than when it is sent cold.

Contactability is gated by consent flags: never count or target customers with dnd_flag set, and respect email/SMS/push opt-ins. Reachable base, not total base, is the correct denominator for campaign reach and conversion.

Card upgrades show up as UPGRADED_TO events in card_lifecycle_events. To measure post-upgrade spend lift, compare a card's monthly transaction value for the three months before vs. after the upgrade event.

A utility/rent surcharge applies only to transactions on or after 15 January 2026 (surcharge_levied_inr). Any analysis of surcharge revenue or its spend impact must filter to that date onward, or it will understate per-transaction surcharge.

Cross-sell whitespace = cardholders who hold no other bank product (no SAVINGS/SALARY/FD/loan in product_holdings). These single-product customers are the highest-value targets for deepening the relationship.

Rewards economics: points liability and redemption rate (rewards_summary) directly affect card profitability. Points expiring in 90 days are a natural nudge trigger; high unredeemed balances signal disengagement risk.
Industry benchmark: Indian credit-card revolve rates run materially below the US (~40–50%); a 25–35% revolve rate is healthy for an Indian issuer. This portfolio's 27.6% sits squarely in that band.

Industry benchmark: lifecycle/cross-sell campaign conversion typically lands at 1–3% for credit-card portfolios; RM-assisted (phone) channels convert several times higher than SMS or email. Compare per-channel conversion against this range before judging a campaign.

Industry benchmark: average credit utilization of 10–30% is considered healthy; utilization persistently above ~80% is an early delinquency signal. The portfolio average of 12.5% is low and conservative.
Dormancy is a leading indicator of attrition. A card with no purchase transactions for 90+ days (DORMANCY_ONSET propensity event) should be flagged for reactivation before it moves to CLOSED.
When computing spend, exclude non-purchase transaction types (REFUND, REVERSAL, FEE, AUTOPAY) and filter response = 'APPROVED'. Including reversals or declines double-counts or inflates spend.

CIBIL band and monthly-income band are the primary credit-quality segments. Higher CIBIL/income cohorts justify higher limits, premium products, and EMI offers, while lower bands warrant tighter limits — always segment growth campaigns by these before recommending an offer.
